posts.title: The Download: AI’s self-improvement problem, and what’s driving the heat
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. AI’s recursive self-improvement might not come so quickly after all The AI industry’s boldest promise right now is that AI will soon improve itself, with almost no need for human oversight.…
bullets: New research indicates that AI agents currently lack the creativity and judgment required for open-ended research, casting doubt on the immediate feasibility of autonomous recursive self-improvement.
OpenAI has paused development on its Astra model after it crossed a 'critical' safety risk threshold, highlighting a divergence in safety strategies compared to competitors like Anthropic.

Global climate patterns are intensifying, with record-breaking heat waves in the US, Europe, and South Korea; experts warn that the ongoing El Niño cycle could lead to even higher temperatures in 2027.
The humanoid robotics sector is showing extreme market volatility, evidenced by Chinese manufacturer Unitree’s stock surging 629% during its recent IPO.

posts.title: Apple Settles With E.U., U.S. App Store Fees, ATT Rules in Germany
posts.summary: Apple's App Store is finally facing the reality of lower fees, and the EU should be satisfied with its work; it's ok it's late.
bullets: Apple has reached a settlement regarding its App Store fee structure, signaling a significant shift in its long-standing business model under regulatory pressure.
The European Union's regulatory efforts have successfully forced Apple to concede on fee structures, marking a major milestone in the ongoing antitrust battle against the company's ecosystem.
The implications of these settlements extend beyond the EU, as Apple faces concurrent pressure in the U.S. and new regulatory rulings regarding App Tracking Transparency (ATT) in Germany.
This development represents a fundamental change in how Apple monetizes its platform, potentially impacting future revenue streams and the competitive landscape for third-party developers.

posts.title: The Future Of AI Compute Won’t Run On Just One Kind Of Chip
posts.summary:
Power, token cost, interconnects, and software orchestration are pushing data centers toward heterogeneous clusters built from CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, optics, and custom accelerators.
The post The Future Of AI Compute Won’t Run On Just One Kind Of Chip appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Data center architectures are shifting toward heterogeneous clusters that integrate CPUs, GPUs, NPUs, and custom accelerators to handle the increasing complexity of AI workloads.
Scaling AI performance beyond a single machine requires significant innovations in high-speed interconnects and software orchestration to manage workload placement effectively.
Memory bandwidth and HBM utilization have emerged as critical bottlenecks, as the dynamic nature of model context and request volume places extreme pressure on existing hardware.
Hyperscalers are currently leading the development of infrastructure that optimizes VM placement and high-speed networking to achieve linear scaling in large-scale AI environments.

posts.title: Seres swings to H1 loss on parts price hikes, asset impairment
posts.summary:
The average daily price of battery-grade lithium carbonate jumped 132.2% in H1, while chips saw structural shortages and sharp price increases.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Seres reported a net loss of 1.72 billion yuan for H1 2026, a sharp reversal from the 2.94 billion yuan profit recorded in the same period last year.
Profitability was severely impacted by a 132.2% surge in battery-grade lithium carbonate prices and structural shortages in automotive-grade chips.
The company booked a 1.75 billion yuan impairment on intangible assets, reflecting the rapid pace of technological iteration in the NEV sector.

posts.title: China NEV retail sales fall 15% in first 16 days of August, outperforming broader market
posts.summary:
NEV retail sales totaled 399,000 units from August 1-16, with retail penetration at 63.6%.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: China's NEV retail sales reached 399,000 units in the first 16 days of August, representing a 15% year-on-year decline but a 1% increase from the previous month.
NEVs maintained a strong market share, accounting for 63.6% of total passenger vehicle retail sales during the period.
The broader automotive market is struggling, with total passenger vehicle retail sales down 22% year-on-year, driven by a collapse in demand for gasoline-powered vehicles.
